sections.heading: Ocean.io limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer; Credit minimums and yearly packaging require modeling before comparing to seat tools; Native email outreach/sequencing depth is limited because it forces process changes or add-ons around Ocean.io when prospecting is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Credits (yearly minimum) with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain contact data at the expense of Data depth / intent specialization vs outreach execution built-in — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Credits (yearly minimum) · contact data | Custom.

Alternative context: unlike Clay, Ocean.io is preferable when GTM teams whose primary job is finding lookalike / similar companies to best customers because prospecting plus contact data match; prefer Clay when Buyers who need a full contact database + sequencer as the primary seat because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Ocean.io
sections.body:
Scenario: for prospecting teams, recommend Ocean.io when GTM teams whose primary job is finding lookalike / similar companies to best customers; recommend an alternative path when Buyers who need a full contact database + sequencer as the primary seat because Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer dominates.

Implementation effort: setup takes a named admin for prospecting plus a freeze window if HubSpot are in the cutover path.

Integrations in research: HubSpot, Salesforce.

Final call: proceed with Ocean.io when prospecting plus contact data outweigh Lookalike/similar-company specialist — not a full contact mega-database or sequencer; walk when Buyers who need a full contact database + sequencer as the primary seat because workarounds will eat the Credits (yearly minimum) spend.
